newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots down.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots down.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market closed mostly up on Monday due to new issues in the stock markets while the impact of the ban on state banks from trading on the repo market had faded, traders said.
The annual rate for the most active seven-day contract rocketed to 17.00 percent from 11.50 percent last Friday.
Total turnover rose to 10.82 million lots from 7.79 million. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Traders said the impact of the ban on state banks trading on the repo market, which hit most of the early-maturing rates last week, had been digested.

Meanwhile, the new issue of Guizhou Hualian (Group) Co Ltd and the listing of Tianjin Zhongchu Commerce & Trade Stock Co Ltd triggered some institutions to borrow funds, which helped to push up the early-maturing contracts, a local trader said.
Meanwhile, contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly down.

The most active 10-year bond fell more than one yuan due to the high return of the new two-year treasure to be issued on Friday, which indicated a cut in bank interest rates is unlikely in the short term, they said.
The bond that matures in 1999, the market barometer, fell to 115.39 yuan from 116.43 yuan last Friday, on volume of 0.68 billion yuan today.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market fell to 1.16 million lots from 1.33 million.
The price of the new two-year bond which goes on sale on Friday has been set at 82.39 yuan, higher than the market expectation.
"It was bad news for some investors who had believed the central bank would cut bank interest rates in the short term, and that triggered heavy institutional selling today," one trader said.
The contracts were also affected by the announcement last week that state banks would be prohibited from trading T-bills on credit, said a second trader.
Traders expect the spot rates to rally slightly following today's big losses.
